points.body: During prehistoric times, wild animals abounded in the Shivaliuṋga mountain range. The wild animals of ancient India lived in greater numbers in this mountain range than in Ráŕh. This chapter of history was written even before the emergence of human beings on earth. The era when humans first appeared on earth was no longer the era of very large forest animals. It is noticeable that, apart from large-sized mammoths, the majority extremely large-sized animals of prehistoric times lived in the Shivalinga mountain range. Giraffes, dinosaurs, hippos and zebras all lived there. Before Gondwanaland became partially submerged in the sea, and after the rise of the Himalayas from the ocean depths, these forest animals were linked by land with Africa. Later, when large parts of Gondwanaland went under the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean, the animals were separated from Africa, their original homeland. Since the Indian climate was not conducive to their survival, and also due to human aggression, they were obliterated from the face of the earth. Animals of the prehistoric era that lived in Ráŕh (Ráŕh was part of Gondwanaland) were likewise massacred by human beings.

The Garo hills were formerly part of the zamindary estate of the Susangh kings of Mymensingh. The British separated it, however, and made it a district of Assam. points.body: From a sociological analysis, Kháshi region has distinctive traits. In most parts of India, patrilineal lineage and inheritance systems are in vogue. The only exceptions are Bauṋgálistán, Kerala and Kháshi. In Bauṋgálistán, the family system is patrilineal, but the inheritance system is partly matrilineal and partly patriarchal. As per natural law, a Bengali son inherits the property of a childless maternal uncle according to Dáyabhága [the Bengali system of inheritance]. Yet, in north India, according to the Mitákśará [an ancient Hindu treatise on the laws and rules of inheritance] system, the nephew does not inherit the property of the maternal uncle. In Kerala, both the family and inheritance systems have patrilineal and matrilineal influences. In other words, a child born of a Brahman father and a Kayastha [Nayar] mother would be known by its motherʼs caste [Nayar]. Generally, the child would use the title of its mother. That is, the matrilineal influence is much greater among the Keralite Nayars (in this context, the Nayar regulations are noteworthy) than among the Kayasthas of Bengal.

In this manner, due to continuous landslides, one after another, a gartta (gr + kta = gartta) [pit] is formed across the stretch of the hills. In the correct grammatical spelling of gartta, there should be double t-s, but according to the rules of pronunciation or phonetics of ancient times, the rśis used to pronounce the word grttr (g-r-r-r-t-t-a). However, this difficult pronunciation did not last long. In the course of time the pronunciation metamorphosed into gartta. As per the rules for the doubling of letters, the spellings garta and gartta are both equally correct, but not grta, because r or rr, whichever is there in the previous consonant, will be used as r at the top of the second consonant. points.body: Later, the Vedic derivative of the word dvigarttabhúmi was duggarbhúmi, and still later it became d́uggarbhúmi. From d́uggarbhúmi came the expression D́ográ desh [land of the D́ogra people], which is another name for Jammu; the language of the land is D́ogri, and the people are known as D́ográ. Thus, in this manner, when cavities are formed across the hillsides, they are called guhás (caves). Another meaning of guhá is a similar place within the mind. Just as people take shelter inside caves, similarly souls obtain refuge inside the caves of the mind.

points.body: When hill caves or crevices are decoratively remodeled to serve as religious sites, it is called gumphá. Many caves of the Himalayas are such Buddhist gumphás. The English word for guhá is cave. When a cave, due to continuous earthquakes, or as a result of being struck with axes or chisels by humans, becomes longer and longer in length and gradually takes the form of a long tunnel, it is called cavern in English. People of prehistoric times used to live in caves and gumphás, but they always preferred to live in caverns, because each cavern could not only accommodate several families, it also provided greater security. One of the insignias of human civilization is painting, which is the earliest carrier of its culture, its original identity. Just as the people of ancient times traced line drawings in these caverns and drew images of social and family life, similarly they sketched images with the subtle faculties of their mind. Thence came the ancient cave drawings of Ajanta, Elora, the underground cave sketches in the hills near Kota [Rajasthan] and the drawings in the Khirkhiria hills of Mungher district. The cultural imprint of prehistoric times, when human history had not yet been created, was portrayed through these cave drawings, since there were no books or scripts. Just as there used to be long ports by the rivers, there were also long caverns along and in the hills. These long caverns were called girikandaras. ( 2 )

It was a widely used Sanskrit word in medieval times. In the Puranic age, the word Saurashtra was concurrently used for the entire Gurjar. Anga-Vauṋga-Kaliuṋga Saoráśt́reśu-Mágadheśu ca.

points.body: Tantra has chiefly two branches – the Kashmir branch and the Bengal branch. The Kashmir branch was practiced to the west and north of Kashmir – Gándhár, Áryańyavraja or Iran, Arabia, Mesopotamia, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Mongolia, Outer Mongolia (China) and a large part of Siberia. The Shaeva, Shákta and other schools of Tantras were practiced in accordance with the Kashmirii system in all these places. Even now you will see in these countries instances of phallus worship, meditation on dead bodies, dancing and jumping with dead corpses (in the Kurmun village of Burdwan district, the last vestige of this Shaivite ritual were found centering around the Ishaneshvar temple. In Burdwan and Birbhum, especially in Ajay valley near Katwa, the Bolan festival held there is a Shaivite celebration). The other branch of Tantra, namely, the practice of the Bengal branch [of Tantra] is prevalent in the rest of India and the rest of the world. For example, Jammu, Punjab, Northern India, Western India, Nepal, Tibet, China, Japan, Bhutan, Vauṋga, and Kamrup. Regarding this Gaoŕiiya Tantra or Váuṋglá Tantra above words have been said [in the previous page]. ( 3 )

points.body: In the annals of human history, many truths and falsehoods have been recorded. Attempts have been made to belittle the importance of great personalities, to erase them from the pages of history, and often small and insignificant people have been magnified and presented as great. But none of these attempts has been successful. Everything is written on the pages of eternal time exactly as it happened; the selfish and vain efforts of petty people have left behind only scornful mirth and derisive laughter on the vast canvas of eternal time.

Though the Supreme Entity is not only a witnessing entity – He is much more than that – still He is the uninvolved witness of all the sequences of events.

His witness-ship does not involve Him in any event –Kleshakarmavipákásháyaeráparámrśt́ah Puruśavisheśa Iishvarah [“The special Puruśa who remains unassailed by afflictions, actions, reactions, and saḿskáras, is Iishvara, the Lord”].
points.body: This colourful pageant of history, these unknown pictures of the past, the variegated splendour of this theatrical show, are all every moment rising and falling on the bosom of eternity. History is merely giving a gentle blow, a soft vibration of existence, on the solid rock of time. It has been said, Teśáḿ vilakśańo sákśii [“He is the witness with opposite characteristics”]. Paramashiva, Supreme Consciousness, is intimately associated with all the various scenes of the acts of history, past, present and future: He is their impartial witness. Though the Supreme Entity is not only a witnessing entity – He is much more than that – still He is the uninvolved witness of all the sequences of events. He does not distort history, nor does He give undue importance to any matter or any entity. He is outside the scope of the law of causation, so He is the witness with “opposite characteristics” ( 1 ) to all occurrences. His witness-ship does not involve Him in any event –Kleshakarmavipákásháyaeráparámrśt́ah Puruśavisheśa Iishvarah [“The special Puruśa who remains unassailed by afflictions, actions, reactions, and saḿskáras, is Iishvara, the Lord”]. ( 2 )
